correctness.rationale: The exact Laurent substitution x=(a+a⁻¹)/2, y=(b+b⁻¹)/2, z=(λ/(ab)+ab/λ)/2 verifies the sextic. It is monic quartic in z. For generic x,y, choosing the two lifts of each gives four distinct z-values: equality of two half-traces requires equality or inversion of their lifts, and the latter is not an identity for opposite choices since λ²≠1. Thus the irreducible torus image accounts for all generic roots; monicity rules out a vertical factor and distinctness rules out a power. W=0 cuts the Cartier hyperplane section, given in its plane by 4X²Y²Z², and its support has zero ambient gradient. On a nonvertex line chart the exact normal discriminant is 16t²(c²−1)(1−t²)²; when it is nonzero, analytic splitting in the two normal variables gives transverse branches. At a side point put X=cW+u, Y=1, Z=1+t: the degree-two and degree-three terms are 4u² and 8tu². The critical u-section starts in degree three, so the quartic residual comes from setting u=0 and is 4(1−c²)t²W². At a vertex, the critical W-section starts with 2cyz, leaving quartic 4(1−c²)y²z². In both cases the two verified singular axes force the residual and its derivatives to vanish on each axis, giving divisibility by the product of their squares. The quartic coefficient is nonzero; taking an analytic square root of the remaining unit yields U²−V²T². Even sign changes and permutations give the nine exhaustively. The two intersection curves are transverse within either smooth branch.
residual_risks: The notation for the doubled lines denotes the planar intersection scheme and its multiplicities; it does not assert each line on the singular surface is individually Cartier.

The proof uses c²≠1 in the local jet argument. The exclusion of c=0 defines the stated scope but is not shown to be necessary for this boundary calculation, despite the stronger wording in the limitations. No excluded phase or global normalization is needed for the verdict.

value.rationale: The ordinary projective closure is a natural geometric object, and the type of its boundary singularities is not encoded by the multiplicities of the planar section alone. A researcher studying its local normalization or resolving its boundary needs to know where double curves meet and whether the two local branches stay separate or pinch. The uniform and exhaustive nine-point classification answers exactly that question beyond the already studied affine singularities.
residual_risks: Not a global normalization, conductor or resolution computation.
